question: The loss of MHC class I makes the cells susceptible to lysis by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Loss of MHC class I -> decreased recognition by Tc lymphocytes -> increased susceptibility to lysis by Tc lymphocytes -> 95% CHAIN: Loss of MHC class I -> increased susceptibility to lysis by NK lymphocytes -> 90% CHAIN: Loss of MHC class I -> reduced antigen presentation to Tc lymphocytes -> decreased Tc lymphocyte activation -> 95%
enhanced_information: Loss of MHC class I leads to decreased recognition by Tc lymphocytes, increasing susceptibility to lysis by Tc lymphocytes. Additionally, loss of MHC class I increases susceptibility to lysis by NK lymphocytes. Macrophages and Th lymphocytes are not directly involved in the lysis of cells lacking MHC class I. Complement is not primarily responsible for the lysis of cells due to MHC class I loss.
analysis: The core medical principle is that the loss of MHC class I makes cells susceptible to lysis by both NK lymphocytes and Tc lymphocytes. While Tc lymphocytes are the primary cells responsible for recognizing and lysing cells lacking MHC class I, NK lymphocytes also play a role in this process. Macrophages and Th lymphocytes are not directly involved in this lysis, and complement is not the primary mechanism for cell lysis in this context.
